Its portfolio of starch, starch derivatives, edible oils, de-oiled cakes, feed ingredients and yarn serves food and beverages, pharmaceuticals, paper, textiles, animal nutrition, construction chemicals and industrial customers, from multinationals and large corporates to MSMEs and small vendors. risks.note: Identified by the Company as the most material risk for an agro-processor. Volatility in agricultural commodity prices escalates input costs, pressures margins and swings working capital. Managed through diversified and regional procurement, seasonal buying strategies, selective hedging, market monitoring, inventory planning, efficient warehousing, and partly offset by yield, efficiency and product-mix improvements.
risks.risk: Raw material and commodity price volatility (maize, oilseeds, cotton)

risks.note: Pressure on pricing, margins and market share in a largely commodity-linked product set. Mitigation rests on product quality, customer servicing, value-added and application-led offerings, long-standing customer relationships, plus capacity expansion, process efficiency and product diversification.
risks.risk: Competitive intensity across starch, starch derivatives, agro-processing and textile markets

risks.note: Exports contribute 31.56% of total turnover across 66 countries, so geopolitical tensions, trade restrictions, freight volatility and weaker international demand translate directly into lower export volumes, higher logistics cost and uncertain customer orders. Mitigated by serving both domestic and export markets, tracking global trade developments and proactive logistics management.
risks.risk: Export concentration and geopolitical / trade disruption

risks.note: Delay or lower-than-expected utilisation of newly commissioned capacity and new platforms would mean lower return on capital employed, a longer fixed-cost absorption period and slower contribution from new capacities. Managed via phased commissioning, technical stabilisation, product testing, customer approvals and market development, leaning on established maize-processing capability and the existing customer network for absorption.
risks.risk: Capacity ramp-up and new product platform execution, including fermentation-led products

risks.note: Rising temperatures, erratic monsoons and more frequent extreme weather affect yields, quality and availability of maize and soybean sourced across multiple Indian regions, causing supply-chain disruption and price volatility; BRSR flags negative financial implications from higher procurement cost and additional climate-resilience investment. Mitigated through a diversified PAN-India sourcing network, stronger procurement planning and supplier engagement, and greater renewable energy use.
risks.risk: Climate change and crop-yield variability in the agricultural feedstock base

risks.note: Water is critical across manufacturing and the agricultural value chain; rising water stress, changing rainfall and declining groundwater levels threaten operating continuity and raise freshwater procurement cost. The Company has commissioned a dedicated pipeline to a government water source about 50 km away at one major facility (investment of around Rs 20 Crores) and is evaluating similar approaches elsewhere, alongside conservation, efficiency and groundwater recharge.
risks.risk: Water stress and dependence on groundwater at manufacturing sites

risks.note: Volatility in power and fuel prices raises manufacturing cost, particularly in energy-intensive maize and starch-derivative operations. Countered by investment in renewable energy, biomass and biogas, solar installations, agro-fuel based boilers and energy-efficiency initiatives that also present an upside opportunity through lower long-term cost.
risks.risk: Energy cost and availability in energy-intensive processing

risks.note: Evolving food safety, environmental, labour, product quality and export regulations require continuous monitoring; non-compliance or a quality failure could bring penalties, product recalls, export restrictions, operational disruption and reputational damage, while strong compliance conversely improves export readiness and customer confidence. Addressed through a compliance-oriented framework, regulatory monitoring, robust documentation, periodic compliance audits, employee training, quality assurance systems and testing protocols.
risks.risk: Regulatory, food-safety and product-quality compliance in a highly regulated export-facing sector
